result.title: Phase-Conditioned Reward Shaping for Token-Efficient LLM Reasoning
result.summary: Extended reasoning can help language models solve complex problems, but long responses often contain both useful computations and redundant checks. Conventional length penalties encourage shorter responses without distinguishing the functions of intermediate steps. We propose Phase-Conditioned Reward Shaping (PCRS), a framework that combines phase identification with training-time reward allocation. We investigate two classification routes: PCRS-H with a hidden-state classifier and PCRS-T with a frozen text classifier. Our main text classifier implementation assigns overlapping reasoning, execution, and revision labels to native chunks, then uses these labels and exact repetition to adjust existing token penalties. We compare the completed configurations on six mathematical and scientific reasoning benchmarks and examine four reward-weight settings with the text classifier. Compared with a baseline using token-level length penalties, the default text classifier configuration reduces mean response length by 3.13%; sampled Pass@1 is approximately 62.07% for both methods, while oracle Pass@16 rises from 86.08% to 87.67%. These results show how phase-informed penalty allocation can reduce output volume and improve multi-attempt coverage without inference-time classification.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Phase-Conditioned Reward Shaping：用隐藏状态分类器或冻结文本分类器把推理过程标为 reasoning／execution／revision 阶段，再按阶段与重复检测调整 token 级长度惩罚，在六个数学与科学基准上比较不同奖励权重配置。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本工作，无视觉或 latent 状态，但「按阶段分配奖励、区分有用计算与冗余检查」的训练期贡献分配思路，可能为 LVR 中各推理步（含停止与复查步）的监督权重与 token 预算控制提供可核查线索；增益有限（平均长度约降 3.13%），优先级偏低。
